name: Build and Deploy

# =============================================================================
# DEPLOYMENT FLOW:
#   Push to any branch except main  ->  lint + typecheck only (PR gate, no deploy)
#   Push to main (after PR merge)   ->  build image, deploy directly to PROD
#
# No dev environment/Container App: this repo's actual usage is a single
# perpetual feature branch (see copy-blob.yml — force-pushed as a full
# snapshot each sync, PR'd into main). The code already lint/tsc-checked on
# that branch push is bit-for-bit what lands on main after merge, so main's
# push does NOT re-run lint/tsc — it goes straight to build+deploy. If your
# workflow ever changes to allow direct pushes to main outside a PR, add the
# check back for main too.
#
# HOW AZURE AUTH WORKS (OIDC - no stored passwords):
#   The deploy job sets the "prod" GitHub Environment.
#   GitHub signs the OIDC token with subject = "repo:OWNER/REPO:environment:prod".
#   Azure AD has a federated credential that trusts that exact subject.
#   `az acr login` (after azure/login) reuses that same OIDC session to fetch a
#   short-lived ACR token — no ACR admin password stored anywhere.
#
# CONFIGURE: change these env vars if your Azure resource names differ.
# =============================================================================

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review]
  push:
    branches: [main]

permissions:
  id-token: write
  contents: read

env:
  RESOURCE_GROUP:     skillos-eus2-rg
  CONTAINER_APP_NAME: skillos
  IMAGE_NAME:         skillos

# Required GitHub Secrets (Settings -> Secrets -> Actions):
#   AZURE_CLIENT_ID        AZURE_TENANT_ID        AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID
#   ACR_NAME               ACR_LOGIN_SERVER
#   DATABASE_URL           AUTH_SECRET            CONFIG_ENCRYPTION_KEY
#   NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN (optional)
#
# Note: DATABASE_URL/AUTH_SECRET/CONFIG_ENCRYPTION_KEY are pushed here as
# GitHub secrets by `azure-setup.ps1 -Deploy` for reference/redundancy only -
# this workflow does not itself set them as Container App env vars on every
# deploy (that's a one-time azure-setup.ps1 step, see CLAUDE.md).
#
# Also required by .github/workflows/cron-scheduler.yml (not this workflow):
#   SITE_URL     — the deployed site's own base URL, used to build the cron
#                  endpoint URLs (e.g. https://your-domain.com). Renamed from
#                  NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL (2026-08) — it was never actually
#                  consumed client-side (that prefix triggers Next.js to bake
#                  a var into the browser bundle, which nothing here needed);
#                  it only fed a GitHub Actions curl target and a couple of
#                  server-only Node fallback chains, so the NEXT_PUBLIC_
#                  prefix was a stale, misleading name for a plain secret.
#   CRON_SECRET  — must match the CRON_SECRET value set in Admin Central
#                  (Cron Jobs section) — see lib/configCatalog.ts.

jobs:

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Runs only for pull requests targeting main — the PR gate. No Azure login,
  # no deploy.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  check:
    name: Lint and TypeCheck
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "22"

      # Output suppressed unless it fails — install success/failure is all that
      # matters here; Lint/TypeScript check below stay fully verbose since
      # every violation they report is exactly what this job exists to surface.
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          npm install > /tmp/install.log 2>&1 && \
            echo "Finished: npm install OK ($(wc -l < /tmp/install.log) lines of output suppressed)" || \
            (echo "FAILED: npm install — full output below"; cat /tmp/install.log; exit 1)

      - name: Lint
        run: npm run lint

      - name: TypeScript check
        run: npx tsc --noEmit

      # 2026-09-17 fix: no dependency vulnerability scanning existed anywhere
      # in CI. Deliberately non-blocking (`|| true`) for now — this repo has
      # no committed lockfile yet (a separate, already-tracked gap), so
      # `npm audit` here runs against whatever versions `npm install` above
      # happened to resolve, not a pinned/reviewed set. Surfacing findings is
      # useful immediately; failing the build on them isn't safe to turn on
      # until a lockfile exists and someone's triaged the current baseline.
      - name: Dependency vulnerability scan (advisory only)
        run: npm audit --audit-level=high || true

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Runs only when a PR into main is merged. Build (cached) + push +
  # deploy straight to PROD.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  deploy:
    name: Build & Deploy to PROD
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    environment:
      name: prod

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Azure login
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          client-id:       ${{ secrets.AZURE_CLIENT_ID }}
          tenant-id:       ${{ secrets.AZURE_TENANT_ID }}
          subscription-id: ${{ secrets.AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID }}

      - name: ACR login (OIDC session — no stored ACR password)
        run: az acr login --name ${{ secrets.ACR_NAME }}

      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3

      - name: Build and push image (cached)
        uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
        with:
          context: .
          push: true
          tags: |
            ${{ secrets.ACR_LOGIN_SERVER }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ github.sha }}
            ${{ secrets.ACR_LOGIN_SERVER }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:latest
          build-args: |
            NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN=${{ secrets.NEXT_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN }}
          cache-from: type=gha
          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max

      # Self-healing: the Container App's managed identity needs AcrPull on the
      # registry or every image pull fails with an opaque UNAUTHORIZED error.
      # azure-setup.ps1 grants this at creation time, but the identity lookup
      # immediately after `containerapp identity assign` can race Azure's
      # control plane and silently miss the grant (see azure-setup.ps1's
      # EnsureAcrPullAccess comment for the full root cause). Running this
      # idempotent check on every deploy means it self-heals automatically
      # instead of requiring a manual azure-setup.ps1 re-run.
      - name: Ensure ACR pull access for Container App
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -e
          APP="${{ env.CONTAINER_APP_NAME }}"
          RG="${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }}"
          ACR_NAME="${{ secrets.ACR_NAME }}"

          ACR_ID=$(az acr show --name "$ACR_NAME" --resource-group "$RG" --query id --output tsv)

          PRINCIPAL_ID=""
          for i in $(seq 1 6); do
            PRINCIPAL_ID=$(az containerapp show --name "$APP" --resource-group "$RG" --query "identity.principalId" --output tsv 2>/dev/null || true)
            if [ -n "$PRINCIPAL_ID" ] && [ "$PRINCIPAL_ID" != "None" ]; then break; fi
            echo "Waiting for managed identity to propagate ($APP, attempt $i/6)..."
            sleep 10
          done

          if [ -z "$PRINCIPAL_ID" ] || [ "$PRINCIPAL_ID" = "None" ]; then
            echo "::warning::Could not retrieve managed identity for $APP - AcrPull may be missing. Deploy will likely fail to provision."
          else
            EXISTING=$(az role assignment list --assignee "$PRINCIPAL_ID" --role AcrPull --scope "$ACR_ID" --query "[0].id" --output tsv 2>/dev/null || true)
            if [ -z "$EXISTING" ]; then
              echo "Granting AcrPull to $APP's managed identity..."
              az role assignment create --assignee "$PRINCIPAL_ID" --role AcrPull --scope "$ACR_ID" --output none
            else
              echo "AcrPull already granted to $APP's managed identity."
            fi

            REGISTRY_SET=$(az containerapp registry list --name "$APP" --resource-group "$RG" --query "[?server=='${{ secrets.ACR_LOGIN_SERVER }}'].server" --output tsv 2>/dev/null || true)
            if [ -z "$REGISTRY_SET" ]; then
              echo "Attaching registry via system identity..."
              az containerapp registry set --name "$APP" --resource-group "$RG" --server "${{ secrets.ACR_LOGIN_SERVER }}" --identity system --output none
            fi
          fi

      # 2026-09-17 fix: captured BEFORE deploying so a failed post-deploy
      # health check below has something concrete to roll back to. Read-only
      # (az containerapp show), so this cannot itself affect the running app —
      # worst case on a query-syntax mismatch is an empty/missing output,
      # which the rollback step below explicitly checks for before acting.
      - name: Capture currently-deployed image (for rollback)
        id: previous_image
        shell: bash
        run: |
          PREV=$(az containerapp show \
            --name           "${{ env.CONTAINER_APP_NAME }}" \
            --resource-group "${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }}" \
            --query          "properties.template.containers[0].image" \
            --output         tsv 2>/dev/null || true)
          echo "image=$PREV" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Previously-deployed image: ${PREV:-<none found>}"

      - name: Deploy image
        shell: bash
        run: |
          az containerapp update \
            --name           "${{ env.CONTAINER_APP_NAME }}" \
            --resource-group "${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }}" \
            --image          "${{ secrets.ACR_LOGIN_SERVER }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ github.sha }}" \
            --output         none

      # The Container App is first created (azure-setup.ps1) pointing ingress at
      # the placeholder image, which listens on port 80 - not the real app's
      # port 3000. Idempotent: no-op once target-port is already 3000.
      - name: Sync ingress target-port to app's real listening port (3000)
        shell: bash
        run: |
          az containerapp ingress update \
            --name           "${{ env.CONTAINER_APP_NAME }}" \
            --resource-group "${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }}" \
            --target-port    3000 \
            --output         none

      - name: Show deployed URL
        id: deployed_url
        shell: bash
        run: |
          FQDN=$(az containerapp show \
            --name           "${{ env.CONTAINER_APP_NAME }}" \
            --resource-group "${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }}" \
            --query          "properties.configuration.ingress.fqdn" \
            --output         tsv)
          echo "$FQDN"
          echo "fqdn=$FQDN" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # 2026-09-17 fix: previously nothing verified the new revision actually
      # came up healthy before the workflow reported success — a deploy that
      # succeeded at the Azure API level but crashed the app on boot (bad
      # migration, missing env var, runtime exception) shipped straight to
      # 100% of traffic with no automated detection. Retries with a delay
      # since a fresh revision needs time to start serving. Hits the
      # container's own FQDN directly (not a custom domain/CDN in front of
      # it), so this reflects the new revision specifically.
      - name: Post-deploy health check
        id: health_check
        shell: bash
        run: |
          FQDN="${{ steps.deployed_url.outputs.fqdn }}"
          if [ -z "$FQDN" ]; then
            echo "::warning::No FQDN captured — skipping health check."
            echo "healthy=unknown" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            exit 0
          fi
          for i in $(seq 1 6); do
            BODY=$(curl -fsS --max-time 15 "https://$FQDN/api/status" 2>/dev/null || true)
            if echo "$BODY" | grep -q '"overall":"operational"'; then
              echo "Health check passed (attempt $i/6)."
              echo "healthy=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
              exit 0
            fi
            echo "Health check attempt $i/6 not operational yet, retrying in 15s..."
            sleep 15
          done
          echo "::warning::Post-deploy health check did not report operational after 6 attempts."
          echo "healthy=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # Best-effort automatic rollback. Deliberately does NOT fail the
      # workflow (no `exit 1`) even if this step itself errors — a rollback
      # attempt that fails leaves the app exactly as broken as it already
      # was, never worse, and a hard workflow failure here wouldn't undo the
      # bad deploy anyway. Treat any ::warning:: from this job as "go check
      # the app manually," same as before this step existed.
      - name: Roll back to previous image on failed health check
        if: steps.health_check.outputs.healthy == 'false'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          PREV="${{ steps.previous_image.outputs.image }}"
          if [ -z "$PREV" ]; then
            echo "::warning::Health check failed and no previous image was captured — manual rollback required. Check the Container App and Sentry now."
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "::warning::Health check failed — rolling back to previous image: $PREV"
          az containerapp update \
            --name           "${{ env.CONTAINER_APP_NAME }}" \
            --resource-group "${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }}" \
            --image          "$PREV" \
            --output         none || echo "::warning::Automatic rollback command failed — manual rollback required. Check the Container App and Sentry now."
